headline: Argentina's possession fortress overwhelms Jordan's disorganised defence
story: Argentina suffocated Jordan from the opening minutes, controlling 68 per cent of possession and dictating play with a suffocating press that forced 42 turnovers. Jordan's three-at-the-back formation offered little resistance to the Argentine midfield's rhythmic movement. By the 31st minute, Messi and Lo Celso had already moved the ball into lethal positions twice; Jordan's sole response was isolation and panic, their 28 per cent possession leaving them reactive, scrambling to recover loose balls in 32.9 seconds to Argentina's brisk 10 seconds.

Argentina's xG of 2.52 to Jordan's 0.96 told the whole story—precision against desperation. Yet Argentina shot themselves in the foot twice: a 28th-minute effort struck the post, and a 90+1 opportunity went begging. Jordan's single goal, courtesy of a 0.52 xG chance at 55 minutes, was merely punctuation to an Argentine masterclass that had already decided the outcome. Argentina's 80th-minute third was a low-xG finish (0.08) off a tired Jordan defence, the match long over by then.

keyMoment.text: Argentina's second goal sealed the contest; Jordan had no answer to the press.

home.verdict: Outmuscled at every press phase; possession hunger must increase before facing elite sides.
points: High-press phases (3.7) were 54% of Argentina's (7.8)—can't defend by conceding midfield.
Only 1 on-target shot from 5 attempts; must sharpen conversion or create fewer, better chances.
Ball recovery in 32.9 seconds versus Argentina's 10—transition defence collapsed; tighten shape.

away.verdict: Possession dominance and press intensity won the day, though finishing cost them late.
points: 68 per cent possession and 42 forced turnovers controlled the match; press intensity (7.8 phases) set the tone.
Post-hit at 28 minutes and 90+1 miss showed wasteful final-third execution; Messi (8.2 rating) salvaged the result.
Conceded one chance (0.52 xG) at 55 minutes—defensive organisation wavered briefly but recovered to kill the game.

statLine: Argentina's 10-second ball-recovery time—32.9 seconds faster than Jordan's—translated to 42 forced turnovers and complete midfield control.
